source.how: read-only: /sys/bus/arm_ffa/devices on a unit running BIOS 5.36_0ACUM027
source.note: no payload was run and nothing was written; sysfs reads only

what_this_is: the FF-A partitions the live firmware enumerates, by partition id and UUID. It is the map the manifests describe and the ACPI methods address.

identifications.0x8003 / 884a63a0-3285-4120-83aa-eec008a: the fan service: this UUID is exactly the two 64-bit constants the DSDT puts in x2/x3 of SMC 0xC400008D, read little-endian. Present on ACUM027.
identifications.0x8003 / 23ea63ed-b593-46ea-b027-8924df8: the RTC service the FFH mailbox in \_SB.FFA0 addresses
identifications.0x8002 / 3cbb7dc8-f848-bc47-222b-9da5966: the Flash Service: the two 16-byte halves of the FLASH manifest's uuid property, i.e. that property is two UUIDs, not one

byte_order_finding: the FLASH manifest stores its two UUIDs in canonical byte order, while STMM's manifest stores its UUID as four **little-endian 32-bit words**: reversing each 4-byte group of 8afb129b64ca47608618c8884caa6c4a gives 9b12fb8a6047ca6488c818864a6caa4c, which is the live value. The vendor data is inconsistent between components, which is why a single decode was wrong before.
consequence: the fan service exists on ACUM027 even though its DSDT declares no FAN0 device, so the module that issues the SMC directly is a candidate there — unproven until a unit answers.
